children: Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) shares fell 3.3% to 190,300 won at the November 17 regular-session close in Seoul, as the Kospi slid 2.59% to 4,968.48, its lowest close in nine months and a fourth straight loss. Foreign investors sold a net 1.44 trillion won of Korean equities. Washington also handed the chipmaker fresh compliance homework.

The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security released an interim final rule, due for publication on November 19, that adds license requirements for advanced chips sent to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. It also narrows how front-end fabricators and packagers can rebut the presumption that advanced logic chips are controlled when the designer is tied to restricted destinations. Reuters reported that Samsung Foundry may face extra customer due diligence and licensing as a result. A US judge also let a DRAM price-fixing class action against Samsung, SK hynix and Micron proceed on November 14.

The rule reads as a compliance burden rather than a direct revenue cut, but it lands just as foreign money exits Korea. GuruFocus gives Samsung a GF Score of 95/100, anchored by a top-ranked balance sheet and strong profitability. Its GF Value of 190,877.55 won sits only 0.3% above the share price, which GuruFocus rates fairly valued, so the selloff has erased the premium rather than created a bargain. The next tests are Nvidia's results tonight and Samsung's December 7 deadline to answer the DRAM complaint.

title: Samsung Stocks Fall 3.3% as Kospi Slides Below 5,000 and US Tightens Foundry Rules
